content.text: Does logic mirror the structure of reality, or only of our language?

content.definition: The view of Russell and the early Wittgenstein that the world is made of simple facts, and a perfect language would match its structure.

examples.title: Form and reality
lines: 'The cat is on the mat' has the form On(Cat, Mat).
Cat and Mat name real things.
examples.note: On this view, a well analyzed sentence pictures a fact.

examples.title: A change of mind
lines: The later Wittgenstein gave up this picture.
examples.note: He came to see meaning in how we use words, not in a hidden logical form.

options: Logic mirrors the structure of reality
question.hint: Atomism pictures the world as made of simple facts.
question.explanation: Logical atomists held that a properly analyzed language mirrors the logical structure of the world.
